# Documents Clause

Manages a keyed collection of documents through preparation, provision, selection and readiness. Each entry has its own preparation record. `start` is a compatibility alias for `prepare`. Selecting a document, making it usable, admitting its parties and requesting cancellation are separate outcomes.

## Configuration

- `bindings.collection` is the required destination: a non-root JSON Pointer. Documents are placed beneath it using the entry's escaped `key`. The collection is registered for embedding.
- `bindings.parties` is an object of party mappings, defaulting to `{}`. Preparation rejects an empty mapping. The mappings participate in resolving template parties against the host's activation roster.
- `bindings.sources` is an object of source bindings by alias, defaulting to `{}`. A binding value of `self` makes candidate parties relevant to admission into the host. Planning merges source declarations from the template's `sources` and its clauses' `parameters.sources`, rejecting conflicting declarations for an alias.
- `bindings.template` is an optional non-root JSON Pointer with no default path. When supplied, its value must exist and is snapshotted during planning. Source-validator planning uses `parameters.template` when present, otherwise the template snapshot.

`parameters.obtain` accepts `create` or `provide`, defaulting to `create`. `provide` requires nonempty `parameters.suppliedBy`, identifying the supplier channel. `parameters.suppliedParties` identifies provider-supplied party slots; a nonempty list is rejected in `create` mode. `parameters.specialization.dataPaths` defaults to `[]` and identifies existing template data slots that may be specialized. These paths cannot overlap or target reserved runtime, clause, source or identity fields.

The stored `prepareFor` controls mode-specific checks. The shown provision logic distinguishes `bootstrap`, which invokes extra access and party checks, from its `inherited` fallback when that stored field is missing. The helper selecting the preparation mode is not supplied, so this fallback does not establish a configuration default.

## Preparation and provision

Preparation uses a nonempty text `key`. The keyed public input declares an explicit key; shared preparation logic falls back to `single` when it is omitted. `requestId` defaults to the key and must also be nonempty. `fields` and `values` each default to `{}` and form part of the preparation intent, together with configuration and template identities.

The `prepare` and `start` preflight classifies an existing entry with identical intent as `duplicate`. Different intent for that entry rejects with `PREPARATION_OBLIGATION_CONFLICT`; an already occupied destination also rejects. The preparation transition hook rejects configuration changes with `PREPARATION_IMMUTABLE_WHILE_OBLIGATIONS_EXIST`.

Preparation stores the constructed `prepared` document and its exact `requirementRef`. In `create` mode it writes that document into the collection, records `documentOrigin` and sets `status` to `selected`. In `provide` mode it records `awaiting_provider` and emits a request to the supplier. That request does not establish that a document has been supplied.

`provide` accepts `document`, `key`, `inResponseTo` and `requirementRef`. Its action defaults read these from the trigger: `key` falls back to `single`, while the other three fall back to empty strings that do not bypass validation. Provision requires an existing `provide` preparation, the recorded supplier channel, and exact request and requirement references.

The candidate must be initialized. Its initialization source and effective clause policy must match the prepared requirement after permitted normalization. Declared slots must satisfy their constraints. Specialized data must remain unchanged between initialization and the supplied publication; parties must pass the applicable identity checks. Undeclared candidate parties and changes to required activation approvals reject. This exact type adds no domain-specific terms or candidate restrictions and returns no domain-specific `nextActions`.

A staged candidate cannot be replaced by a different initialization origin. Once selected, another provision with the same origin is classified as duplicate; a different origin rejects. Provision is blocked for `reapproval_required`, `admission_denied`, `cancellation_requested` and the recognized `cancelled` status.

## Selection and readiness

Runtime records live under `/process_{clauseKey}/entries`, separately from the destination collection. Planning declares an initially empty entries dictionary; missing state is otherwise unknown.

Candidate staging records `candidateOrigin` and `candidateRef`. It can record `admission_pending` when host admission is needed, `awaiting_activation` when the candidate is inactive, or `linking` while required sources lack initialization, roster coverage or activation. A required source with the wrong origin rejects.

A candidate that passes these gates reaches the internal staging result `ready`. Provision then writes its publication reference into the collection and records `selected` with `documentOrigin`; `ready` is not the persisted selection status.

`resume`, destination changes and embedded events invoke refresh. For an initialized selected document, refresh verifies its origin and records `usable` only when activation is true and `namedSourcesReady` passes. It records `selected` when those readiness checks fail, so usability can be withdrawn. If initialization evidence is absent, this refresh branch does not update the recorded status. A transition to usable emits a readiness notification.

Refresh examines entries that already have `documentOrigin`; it does not select staged candidates. A supplier may therefore need to provide the candidate again after admission, activation or linking progresses. `resume` can return `acceptedNew` even without changing an entry.

## Admission, access and cancellation

When a `self` source requires candidate parties missing from the host roster, admission policy is required. Configured admission approvers must be distinct existing host party roles. Admission proposals are processed one at a time. Approver operations require review of the exact document version.

Installation requires an affirmative admission-history marker and matching grant token, `approve` consent from every incoming party, the same host activation revision, and valid access for the expanded roster. Consent operations use incoming parties' lead channels and accept `admissionRef` with `decision` equal to `approve` or `decline`. A decline produces `admission_denied`. An access request can be emitted before installation; `accessRequested` records that request, not successful access provision.

During installation the entry becomes `installing`. Completion verifies host roster coverage, records `admittedRevision` and changes the entry to `linking`. The accompanying event reports `admitted`; this does not establish selection or usability.

A changed activation revision requires `reapproval_required`. A configured approver can rebase using the current `admissionRef` and exact document review. Rebase removes the old token and consents, increments the admission attempt and returns the entry to `awaiting_provider`. Its `reprovision_required` event calls for another provision; that event value is not the stored entry status.

Access registration is exposed on configured party channels. It requires exact document review and a caller channel present in the host party roster, and accepts one to sixteen initialized Timeline Access publications. Installation and detailed access validation are delegated to helpers.

`cancel` requires an existing preparation without `documentOrigin`. It records `cancellation_requested` and emits a cancellation request; repeating it is a duplicate. Once a document is selected, this operation rejects and requires domain-specific cancellation. No supplied transition confirms cancellation as `cancelled`.

## Connected execution

Action connections determine triggers and actors: workflow channels, events, channel messages, document changes, embedded or collection events, initialization, activation and timers. Workflow `party` overrides `channel`. Connection `params` overlays action defaults; false `when` skips execution, while a false configured action condition rejects.

For actions with preflight, only `acceptedNew` proceeds to `before` and the action body. The final `outcome-v1` result must be `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` or `skipped`; only `acceptedNew` proceeds to `after`. `once` defaults to false and, when enabled, is marked fired only after that accepted execution. These outcomes describe action handling, not confirmation of external work.

Timers use either a nonnegative Unix-microsecond `timestamp`, or a timestamped `afterEvent` with positive integer `delayMs` in milliseconds. Relative `policy` defaults to `first`, which ignores later arm triggers once armed; `latest` allows rearming. Absolute timers disallow `delayMs` and `policy`, and relative timers cannot arm from initialization. `cancelOn` emits a timer cancellation request.

The supplied evidence leaves document construction, full template and mode resolution, detailed roster/access checks, readiness-source validation and approval/consent recording to omitted helpers. Their complete acceptance rules are not established here.
